text:
amanda: Ran a long-context KV stress run (65k tokens, continuous generation). Seeing steady memory creep across hosts, looks like fragmentation not freed by GC. attaching quick profile below.

amanda: profile summary:
```
run: 2026-02-18
model: redwood-gptx-22k
workers: 8
duration: 3h
observed: p95 mem +520MB, p99 mem +1.1GB over run
fragmentation metric (small_holes_ratio): 0.22
free_slots: 180/8192
compaction_events: 0 (auto-scrubber off)
```

amanda: root cause hypothesis: allocator leaves many tiny holes (<=512B) when KV caching long contexts; reuse path prefers exact size buckets and doesn't coalesce small neighbors.

ryan: hmm, did anything change in kernel selection/batching last week? last deploy swapped attention kernel to tiled-2 which increased avg seq len, might shift KV access patterns.

amanda: deploy 1766904400 yes, tiled-2 went out. but regression doesn't show CPU spike, just sustained mem drift.

sota: can you dump per-bucket counts? if small-chunk buckets accumulate it points to block-splitting behavior.

amanda: pasted counts:
```
bucket_64: 1240 used, 12 free
bucket_128: 980 used, 8 free
bucket_256: 430 used, 2 free
bucket_512: 60 used, 0 free
bucket_1024+: 15 used, 0 free
small_hole_ratio: 0.22
```

laura: if split-on-alloc is creating many 128/256 fragments then coalescer needs to run more aggressively. Try tuning --kv-compact-threshold and the micro-scrubber interval.

sota: suggested quick experiment params:
`--kv-block-size=4096 --kv-compact-threshold=0.15 --kv-scrub-interval=60s`

dave: ran that config on a canary for 2h. results: reclaimed ~700MB, small_hole_ratio -> 0.08, but p99 latency increased ~6-9% on generation (due to scrubbing work).

amanda: that's promising for memory. do we have a mode that compacts in background with low latency impact? maybe staggered micro-compaction based on idle cycles per-worker.

ryan: idea: colocate compact work on low-priority CPU thread and throttle by generation QPS. If QPS > threshold, pause compaction. Add hysteresis.

laura: also consider merging adjacent small holes when they belong to same allocation epoch instead of waiting for free-slot contiguity. we already track epoch ids on allocations. cheap to check.

sota: caution: contiguous-merge requires defragmenting KV index pointers. risk of pointer churn under concurrency. need a lockless plan or per-shard pause.

amanda: I'll prototype epoch-merge in a branch and run microbench. plan:
1) enable aggressive scrubbing on canary for 4h, collect mem + lat traces
2) implement epoch-merge prototype (off by default)
3) run A/B with kernel tiled-2 and tiled-1 to verify interaction

infra-bot: deploy-canary started for amanda/canary-kv-scrub @ 2026-02-19T03:12:24Z :rocket:

dave: one more datapoint: toggling kv-block-size from 4096 -> 2048 increased fragmentation slightly but reduced per-alloc wasted bytes; tradeoff depends on workload's typical token key sizes.

ryan: sounds like we should add an automated tuning job: sample request key length distribution for tenant and recommend block size & compaction policy. could be part of Optimize.

amanda: agreed. for now I'll push the scrub canary, share traces, and open a small RFC for epoch-merge compaction. will drop results here in ~6h.

laura: :thumbsup: thanks Amanda. short term: enable scrub on low-QPS clusters, monitor p99 latency and small_hole_ratio.

sota: noted. I'll review prototype code when you have it.

amanda: thanks all, posting initial traces in 2h.
